items.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: when he was in his 20s he played trombone with Dixieland groups, including Phil Napoleon

ctx.x: A musical family. My father was a musician. He ended up — well he ended up out of work — but in his heyday he conducted the “Stop the Music” television show and he conducted “Name that Tune,” the original shows back in the ‘50s. And he played, in his day, when he was in his 20s he played trombone with Dixieland groups, including Phil Napoleon and some of those in New York City. So when it came time for me to take music, I took piano at age eight, and when I went into high school at age fourteen I went to Brooklyn…
